title: The ‘goo & prickles’ tweet that became a whole dialect
summary:
visakanv’s 2018 two-liner (“Goo for my prickly friends / Prickles for my gooey friends”) accidentally shipped a whole advice philosophy: stop giving one-size-fits-all takes—give people the *missing* counterbalance. It starts as a cute aphorism, then quickly turns into a reusable brain-module: visakanv formalizes it as two contradictory truths you have to hold at once (“your position is understandable” *and* “you’re out of excuses”), then keeps re-deploying it everywhere—humor vs solemnity (“lighten up” vs “be serious when it counts”), toughness vs tenderness (“let there be toughness in your tenderness”), and productivity takes (“happy idleness for my workaholic friends, material progress for my derelict bum friends”).

Arc is basically: **[trigger: a poetic tweet] → [peak: it becomes a template + a shared vocabulary] → [outcome: people start building with it professionally and socially].** The peak isn’t a fight, it’s the meme escaping containment: tasshinfogleman starts using “prickly” as an identity label and gives the cleanest definitional riff (“goo is sweet/open/nice; prickly is cranky/closed/kind-over-nice”), AskYatharth takes it into astrology brain (“you must cringemaxx and cringeminn at the same time”), and RichDecibels uses it to talk scene-governance and why Visa reads as “rigorous” to some people and “informal” to others (“how I talk is a function of context”). By 2023, Sarah McManus is literally redesigning her coaching brand around “prickles and goo,” citing Alan Watts and turning the dialectic into a practice: helping clients weave both stances.

What sticks afterward is the *format*—people keep stamping new pairs onto it (“therapy for my philosophy friends / philosophy for my therapy friends,” “courage for my strategic friends / strategy for my courageous friends”), and “prickly/gooey” becomes shorthand for calibrating tone, boundaries, and feedback without turning it into moral warfare. If you’ve ever watched advice discourse melt into “be nicer” vs “grow up,” this meme is the cheat code: it hands you a way to say “both, depending,” without sounding like a smug centrist—plus it’s memorable enough that people actually use it.
